Need To Know
Press Pool Protest
ABC, NBC, CBS, and Fox yesterday
suspended TV coverage
of presidential events in response to President Donald Trump barring CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House over reporting he characterized as fake news.
The move came shortly after CNN, MS NOW, and Politico
filed a lawsuit
against Trump, arguing his decision violates the First Amendment. The three banned outlets are members of the White House press pool, alongside ABC, NBC, CBS, Fox, and others. The pool was established in 1937 and has covered every president's daily activities
since Franklin Delano Roosevelt
. Outlets rotate traveling with the president, sharing footage, photos, and quotes with one another. The White House Correspondents' Association has historically selected the pool, but the Trump administration began exerting greater control last year, restricting wire services such as the Associated Press and adding startup media outlets.
Last night, the White House
launched a 24/7 streaming platform
called "Trump TV" to broadcast real-time updates and highlights from major events.

UN General Assembly
The United Nations opens the high-level General Debate of its
81st General Assembly
in New York City today, with speeches from Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and President Donald Trump. Artificial intelligence headlines the agenda for the first time, with the Security Council holding a high-level meeting on the issue tomorrow.
The conflicts in Ukraine, Gaza, and Iran will also be focal points. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will speak tomorrow, seeking support as Russia's invasion enters its fifth year; Russian President Vladimir Putin is absent for the 11th straight year. On Thursday, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas will
speak via prerecorded video after
the US denied him a visa for the second consecutive year. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will speak later that day, with his remarks expected to address Israel's actions in Gaza and Iran. See full speaker schedule
here
The gathering is Guterres’ last as secretary-general. Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan has a narrow lead after three informal polls to succeed him and would become the UN’s first female
secretary-general
if selected.

Swallowable Batteries
MIT researchers have
developed tiny batteries
that can safely dissolve inside the body, potentially expanding the use of ingestible devices. Such devices can monitor vital signs, deliver drugs, or detect medical emergencies, but conventional batteries can pose risks if damaged.
Researchers made two versions: a pencil-eraser-sized disc and a 1-inch-long rectangle (
scroll for photos)
. Both are made from magnesium and molybdenum trioxide (metals considered safe for humans in small amounts), gel, and chemically treated paper wrapped in wax to protect them from the gut. In animal tests, the disc powered a small wireless tracking device that transmitted data from the digestive tract up to 5 feet away; the rectangle powered a stomach-stimulating capsule, boosting a hunger hormone by roughly 50% after 20 minutes.
Separately, tests in simulated stomach fluid found the batteries worked for up to three days before gradually losing power and breaking down within weeks. Researchers have also explored other ways to power swallowed electronics, including
using stomach acid
to generate electricity.
